sources.entry: DailyTxT - Encrypted diary Web application to save your personal memories of each day. Includes a search function and encrypted file upload. (Demo) MIT Docker

summary.one_liner: DailyTxT is a self-hosted, encrypted diary/journal web app written in Svelte and Go, run via Docker, with encrypted entries and file uploads.
summary.what_it_does: DailyTxT lets multiple users write daily diary entries in Markdown with a live preview, tags, and a search across words, tags and filenames. Each user's entries and uploaded files (up to 500 MB each) are encrypted with ChaCha20-Poly1305 before being written to disk, using a per-user key derived from the password with Argon2id. Data is stored as JSON files with no database. Additional features include an image gallery per day, a map for pinning locations and showing GPX tracks, custom templates, a read mode, HTML export, backup and import, and a statistics panel. An admin panel manages users and can temporarily open registration. The app is available in about ten languages and can be installed as a PWA.
use_cases: keep a private encrypted daily journal
self-host a personal diary web app
write and search markdown diary entries
attach photos and files to daily entries
track locations and GPX routes for each day
export or back up personal journal data
how_to_run: Use the docker-compose.yml file in the repository, adjusting environment variables
Generate a secret token with: openssl rand -base64 32 and set SECRET_TOKEN
Set ADMIN_PASSWORD and ALLOW_REGISTRATION as needed
Developers: install Go (1.24+) and Node.js (24+), then run the backend with go build and the frontend with npm install and npm run dev
notable: Server-side encryption of all entries and uploads with per-user keys; no client-side E2E so search still works
Data stored as plain JSON files with no database, for portability
Backup-keys can be used to recover access if a password is lost
Automatic migration from version 1 data when an old user logs in
Supports AMD64 and ARM64 Docker images
caveats: Migrating from version 1 requires following specific steps; updating only the image tag causes server errors
Author states no backward-compatibility guarantee between versions; back up data before updating
